item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Two nitpicks first.

One, the field in the picture looks far, far bigger than 1 x 1.5 km. Two, why can't we just cover the field with an impermeable membrane/canvas or other covering to prevent seeds being able to reach the soil in the first place? Have it inspected for holes and tears once or twice a month, and we should be good, right?

Okay — now. While the effect is somewhat interesting, if a little questionable as far as logistics and and actual execution go, the absolutely absurd amount of redaction and expungement makes reading anything past the second paragraph of the description almost completely pointless. It's nearly impossible to glean any actual information from any of the words you can actually read.

The effect just isn't interesting enough to keep me from downvoting because of that. Sorry.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This. Very much this. Not only do all the expungements and blackouts severely break the flow of the text - almost to the point where it kind of feels like you're reading completely unrelated sentence fragments - but it also ruins the potentially scary implications of the ideas behind them. I mean, yes, I get the choice of fruit, but mentioning third-degree burns and a reverse something-or-other and vague implications of an entity of some sort happening or something…All the expungement there takes it from "Oh god, what could it be?" to just "WTF?" There is potential for a brilliant idea there, but it's too broken up by expungements to really work. As for the blackouts and such during the description of recovery and incident…Meh, it's still pretty heavy-handed, but I kind of get enough of an impression about everything for those parts to work for me.

If I may be so bold as to make a suggestion: Maybe turn the thing-that-might-be-classified-as-a-separate-SCP-that-happens-when-someone-eats-an-apple into SCP-891-1 and write a full-fledged paragraph (or mostly full-fledged paragraph) describing what it is, what it does, and so on. The fact that apple tree saplings seem to spontaneously appear in the field sometimes also suggests that the thing-that-might-be-an-SCP is a very integral part of SCP-891, further justifying turning it into SCP-891-1. I realize that would require a pretty extensive rewrite, and I have nowhere near the skill or authorization needed to do anything about that, but maybe if someone wanted to and the author gave permission…? I really do feel like this could be a great SCP, and I'm really sad that it's sort of ruined by what pretty much amounts to a cop-out (as far as I can tell). :(

All that said, the beginning concept - fruit what makes you eat yourself - is a very good start, and I already like it enough to upvote; I just think that, with some work, it could be a lot better.
